news.headline: Apple Renames Lake Ontario 'Lake America' Because an Executive Order Said So
news.summary: トランプ大統領の行政命令を受け、Appleはカナダとアメリカの国境にあるオンタリオ湖をアメリカ国内のMapsアプリ上で「レイク・アメリカ」に改名した。

commentary: 矛盾: カナダとの国境をまたぐ湖の名前をアメリカ側だけ変えても、湖そのものは1ミリも動かないんですよ。地図の上だけで「俺の湖」にした感じ。
滑稽さ: 行政命令一本で地形の名前が変わるなら、次は「大西洋はトランプ・オーシャン」になっても誰も驚けないじゃないですか。
日本・海外から見ると: カナダ側の地図には今でも「オンタリオ湖」と書いてある。国境のど真ん中にある湖が、岸によって別の名前を持つという、なかなかシュールな状況です。
imagePrompts: A large lake viewed from above, split down the middle by a national border line. The left (US) side is labeled 'LAKE AMERICA' in bold official font. The right (Canadian) side is labeled 'LAKE ONTARIO' in the same font. A tiny Apple logo hovers over the US side with a paintbrush.

A cartographer at a massive wooden desk carefully crossing out 'Ontario' on an antique map and writing 'America' with a quill pen, while a framed executive order hangs on the wall behind him. The map still shows Canada surrounding the lake on three sides.
Two kayakers facing each other in the middle of a lake, one holding a sign reading 'LAKE ONTARIO,' the other holding one reading 'LAKE AMERICA.' A fish jumps between them, completely uninterested.
captions: Apple changed the name of a lake. Canada still has the lake.
MapQuest, which your parents stopped using in 2011, now has more downloads than ChatGPT — because it just didn't rename a lake. That's the whole story.
The executive order changed the map. It did not change the watershed, the fish population, or Canada's opinion of us.
You ever rename half a lake and wonder if the other half got the memo?
Somewhere in Cupertino, an engineer had to open a database, find 'Lake Ontario,' change it to 'Lake America,' close the laptop, and go home for the day. That was the job.
captionsJa: Appleが湖の名前を変えた。湖はカナダにまだある。
2011年に誰もが使うのをやめたMapQuestが、「湖の名前を変えなかっただけ」でChatGPTを抜いて1位になった。それが全部です。
行政命令は地図を変えた。集水域も、魚の数も、カナダの気持ちも、1ミリも変わっていない。
半分だけ名前を変えた湖、残り半分には連絡が届いてないんですけど。
どこかのエンジニアが「オンタリオ湖」を検索して「レイク・アメリカ」に直して、ノートパソコンを閉じて帰宅した。それが今日の仕事。
candidates.newsEn: Apple has renamed Lake Ontario as 'Lake America' for US users of its Maps app, following an executive order from President Trump issued amid his trade dispute with Canada. The lake sits on the border between the US and Canada and has been called Lake Ontario for centuries. The name change applies only to the US version of Apple Maps.

ironyEn.contradiction: The lake hasn't moved an inch, but on the US side of Apple Maps it's now called 'Lake America' — a body of water that is, factually, half Canadian.
ironyEn.absurdity: Apple, a company that once told users 'Think Different,' chose to quietly swap out a name that's been on maps since 1755 because a trade dispute happened.
ironyEn.outside: Canadian users open the same app and still see 'Lake Ontario.' So the lake has two names depending on which shore you're standing on. The water does not care.

ironyEn.contradiction: An executive order about tariffs somehow also became an executive order about Great Lakes nomenclature. The logic connecting those two things has not been made public.
ironyEn.absurdity: Meanwhile, MapQuest — a service most people assumed died in 2009 — shot to No. 1 on the App Store by simply not renaming the lake. Defiance has never required less effort.
ironyEn.outside: From abroad, this reads as a country trying to win a trade war by editing its own map. Canada's exports remain unchanged. The lake's volume remains unchanged. Only the font is different.

news.headline: IRS Fired Its Auditors. Turns Out, Auditors Were the Ones Collecting Taxes.
news.summary: 監察総監のレポートにより、IRS（米国歳入庁）が監査スタッフを大幅削減した結果、税務執行による徴収額が急減していたことが明らかになった。

commentary: 矛盾: 「政府のムダを省く」という名目で税金を集める人員を削ったら、集まる税金が減った。節約しようとして収入を減らすという、家計でもやってはいけないやつ。
滑稽さ: 脱税を摘発する側の人間がいなくなったことで、得をしたのは脱税しようとしていた人たちです。「政府の効率化」の恩恵、これが一番わかりやすい受取人。
日本・海外から見ると: 税務調査官を解雇することで税収が増えると思っていたなら話は別ですが、普通に考えて、チェックする人がいなければ申告は緩くなりますよね。
imagePrompts: An empty government office with rows of vacant desks, audit folders scattered on the floor, and a large scoreboard on the wall showing 'TAX COLLECTED: $0' with a downward arrow. A single plant on one desk is also dead.

A person in a suit walking out of an IRS building carrying a box of belongings, while behind them through the glass doors a line of people with briefcases labeled 'UNPAID TAXES' quietly tiptoe away smiling.

A balance scale: on the left side, a small stack of coins labeled 'SALARY SAVED BY LAYOFFS.' On the right side, a massive pile of gold bars labeled 'TAXES NOW GOING UNCOLLECTED.' The scale is tipped dramatically to the right.
captions: We fired the tax collectors to save money. We are now saving even more money by not collecting taxes.
The Inspector General wrote a report about this. The findings were: yes, if you fire the auditors, people get audited less.
Somewhere, someone who owed the IRS a lot of money just had the best year of their life — courtesy of federal workforce reform.
Government efficiency: achieved. Government revenue: less achieved.
It cost money to run the audit division. It cost more money to stop running it. Nobody put that in the press release.
captionsJa: 節税のために税金を集める人を解雇した。おかげで税金がさらに集まらなくなった。
監察総監がレポートを書いた。内容は「監査する人を解雇したら、監査が減った」。以上。
どこかで税金を大量に滞納していた人が、今年最高の年を過ごしています。連邦政府の効率化のおかげで。
政府の効率化：達成。政府の収入：それほど達成できず。
監査部門の運営にはお金がかかった。廃止するともっとお金がかかった。プレスリリースにはそう書かれていなかった。
candidates.newsEn: The IRS significantly cut its auditing staff last year as part of broader federal workforce reductions. An Inspector General report now shows that tax collections from enforcement efforts have plummeted as a direct result. Consumer and fiscal watchdog groups warn the shortfall could add substantially to the federal deficit.

ironyEn.contradiction: The government cut the people whose job is to collect money from people who aren't paying — and then collected less money. The Inspector General did not seem surprised.
ironyEn.absurdity: In the effort to shrink government spending, the administration eliminated a division that was, by most accounts, generating more revenue than it cost to operate.
ironyEn.outside: Tax authorities in other countries are watching this as a case study. Not a flattering one.

ironyEn.contradiction: Firing enforcement staff to save money is a bit like a restaurant laying off the waitstaff to cut costs and then noticing that revenue has dropped.
ironyEn.absurdity: The people who were supposed to find unpaid taxes are now gone, which means the unpaid taxes are simply staying unpaid. The system is working exactly as gutted.
ironyEn.outside: The Inspector General filed a report. The report found what you'd expect. The question now is what happens to the report.

news.headline: US Mint Sells $1 Trump Coins for $1.55 Each, Which Is Not How a Dollar Works
news.summary: 米造幣局がトランプ大統領の肖像を刻んだ1ドル硬貨を発売。25枚セットで61ドル（1枚あたり約2.44ドル）から販売されており、額面の1.55倍以上の価格設定となっている。

commentary: 矛盾: 1ドルの価値しか持たない硬貨を、政府が1.55ドル以上で売っています。インフレを批判してきた政権が、自分の顔が入った硬貨でインフレを実演してる。
滑稽さ: 25枚買うと61ドル取られるんですが、それを全部使おうとすると25ドルにしかならない。36ドルは「トランプ硬貨プレミアム」として消えていくわけです。
日本・海外から見ると: 日本の造幣局も記念硬貨を額面より高く売ることはありますが、それは「コレクターアイテム」として売るんですよ。これは一応「1ドル硬貨」として売っている。
imagePrompts: A vending machine display case showing a single Trump $1 coin behind glass with a price tag reading '$2.44.' A hand reaches toward it holding a regular dollar bill looking confused.
A scale with a single coin labeled '$1 FACE VALUE' on one side and a price tag reading '$2.44' on the other side, with the price tag side sinking lower. A tiny US Mint logo is stamped on the scale.
A storefront window displaying Trump $1 coins in velvet boxes, with a handwritten sign: 'BUY 100 FOR $154.50 — SPEND THEM AND GET $100 BACK!' A small footnote reads: 'Net loss: $54.50.'
captions: The US government is selling a dollar for $1.55. Inflation, but make it patriotic.
Buy 25 Trump dollars, spend them all, you're out $36. That's not a coin — that's a cover charge.
The face value says $1. The checkout page says $2.44. One of those is lying.
The government is selling money at a markup. The markup is $0.55. The explanation is a coin with a face on it.
For $154.50, you can own $100. The other $54.50 is apparently the cost of the face on the front.
captionsJa: 政府が1ドルを1.55ドルで売っている。インフレ、愛国心でラッピング。
25枚買って全部使うと36ドル損する。これは硬貨じゃなくて入場料です。
額面は1ドル。購入ページには2.44ドル。どっちかが嘘をついてる。
政府がお金を割増価格で売っている。割増分は0.55ドル。理由は、顔の入った硬貨だから。
154.50ドル払えば100ドルもらえる。残りの54.50ドルは、表の顔の使用料らしい。
candidates.newsEn: The US Mint has begun selling President Donald J. Trump $1 coins, priced at $1.55 per coin at minimum. A package of 25 coins costs $61, while 100 coins cost $154.50, making the per-coin price range from $1.545 to $2.44 depending on quantity. The coins have a face value of one dollar.

ironyEn.contradiction: A $1 coin is being sold for $1.55 — by the same government that has made lowering the cost of things a central policy message.
ironyEn.absurdity: If you buy 25 of them and spend them all at a vending machine, you lose $36. The US Mint has found a way to make legal tender a bad investment.
ironyEn.outside: Other countries sell commemorative coins above face value too, but they're usually sold as collectibles. These are officially '$1 coins.' The denomination is right there on the coin.

ironyEn.contradiction: The coin is worth a dollar. The coin costs $2.44 if you buy the small pack. The gap between those two numbers is the entire joke.
ironyEn.absurdity: For $154.50 you receive $100 in spendable currency, a net loss of $54.50, and a very large bag of coins featuring the same face on all of them.
ironyEn.outside: Economists have a word for when the market price of money is higher than its stated value. It's called a 'premium.' Having it on a government-issued product is a choice.

news.headline: Laid Off While on Maternity Leave. It's Legal. It Happens More Than You Think.
news.summary: 育児休暇中にレイオフされた女性が複数おり、CNBCの報道によれば、こうした解雇は違法ではなく、実態として広く行われている可能性がある。

commentary: 矛盾: 産休という「会社の制度を正しく使っている期間」に、同じ会社が「お前はいらなくなった」と伝えられる。制度が制度を食う構図です。
滑稽さ: 「レイオフはビジネス上の判断」と言えば合法になる、というのがアメリカの雇用法のすごいところで、つまり理由の言い方さえ正しければ何でも通る。
日本・海外から見ると: 多くの国では産休・育休中の解雇は原則禁止なんですが、アメリカでは「合法かどうかは文脈次第」という話になる。文脈、重すぎませんか。
imagePrompts: A hospital room seen from the doorway. On the bedside table: a bouquet of congratulatory flowers and a smartphone showing an email notification reading 'RE: Your Position Has Been Eliminated.' The room is empty of people — only the objects tell the story. A balloon in the corner reads 'IT'S A GIRL!'
A corporate HR office with a wall calendar. The weeks labeled 'MATERNITY LEAVE' are circled in red with a sticky note: 'Legally permissible if framed correctly.' The desk is otherwise bare and tidy.

An office desk with two items side by side: a framed photo of a newborn's footprint and a cardboard box labeled 'PERSONAL BELONGINGS.' A sticky note on the box reads: 'Business decision. Nothing personal.'
captions: Great news: you had a baby. Also: we've restructured. Unrelated.
The layoff is legal as long as nobody writes down the real reason. So they don't write down the real reason.
You're protected from being fired for being pregnant. You're not protected from being fired while being on leave for having been pregnant. There's a gap there.
HR calls it a restructuring. You call it from the maternity ward. The timing is, legally speaking, a coincidence.
The benefit is real. The job waiting for you when the benefit ends — that part's optional.
captionsJa: おめでとうございます、出産しました。あと、組織再編しました。無関係です。
本当の理由を書かなければ合法。なので書かない。
妊娠を理由に解雇するのは違法。妊娠で産休中に解雇するのは、状況次第で合法。そこにスキマがある。
会社は「組織再編」と呼ぶ。あなたは産院から電話を受ける。タイミングは、法的には偶然の一致。
産休という制度は本物。産休が終わったときに仕事があるかどうかは、オプション扱い。
candidates.newsEn: Several women have reported being laid off by their employers while on maternity leave. Legal experts note that in many US states, this practice is technically lawful as long as the layoff is framed as a business decision rather than a response to the pregnancy or leave itself. Employment attorneys say the line between legal restructuring and illegal discrimination can be difficult to prove in court.

ironyEn.contradiction: Maternity leave exists so new mothers can keep their jobs while recovering from childbirth. It does not, as it turns out, guarantee that the job will still be there when they get back.
ironyEn.absurdity: The layoff is legal as long as the employer calls it a business decision rather than a pregnancy-related decision. The outcome is identical. The paperwork is different.
ironyEn.outside: In most of Europe, terminating someone during maternity leave requires navigating very specific legal exceptions. In the US, the question is more like: can you prove it was about the baby?

ironyEn.contradiction: Companies offer maternity leave as a benefit. That benefit can be the period during which the company decides to eliminate the position receiving the benefit.
ironyEn.absurdity: Legal experts describe the gap between 'illegal pregnancy discrimination' and 'legal restructuring during leave' as a line that exists mostly in how the HR memo is worded.
ironyEn.outside: The US has no federally mandated paid maternity leave. It does have a law that allows unpaid leave, during which you can still be laid off. That's the system, fully assembled.

news.headline: Uber Cuts 10% of Staff to Move 'Simpler and Faster,' Starting With the Humans
news.summary: Uberが全従業員の約10%を削減すると発表。「よりシンプルかつ迅速に動く」ことを目的とするとしており、小規模チームはほぼ半減、リモートワーク継続を認められるのは全体の約1%にとどまる。

commentary: 矛盾: 人を届けるサービスを提供している会社が、自分の社員を「効率化」という名目でリストラする。ライドシェアのドライバーは業務委託だから「従業員」ではない、というのも含めてなかなかの構図。
滑稽さ: 「シンプルで速い会社になる」という説明で10%カットを発表したんですが、残された人が同じ仕事を10%多くやることを「シンプル」と呼ぶのは、言葉の使い方として勇気がある。
日本・海外から見ると: リモートワーク継続を認めるのが全体の1%というのも地味に厳しくて、オフィス復帰を義務づけつつ同時にレイオフするという、2つのニュースが同時に起きている。
imagePrompts: A large office floor with half the desks empty and chairs stacked on them. Remaining employees sit at their desks with a banner overhead reading 'SIMPLER AND FASTER.' One employee is visibly doing the work of three people, each desk's worth of paperwork stacked in front of them.
An Uber app interface on a phone screen, but instead of requesting a ride it shows a notification: 'Your team has been streamlined. ETA to exit: 2 weeks.' A 4.8-star rating appears below.

A corporate meeting room with a whiteboard. On the whiteboard is written 'HOW TO BE SIMPLER AND FASTER' with a single bullet point: 'Fewer people.' A presenter points to it with a satisfied expression.
captions: Uber laid off 10% of staff to get 'simpler and faster.' The math on who does their work is still loading.
Small teams cut by nearly half. So your four-person team is now a two-person team with four people's tasks. That's not simpler. That's just fewer complaints.
1% of the workforce gets to keep working remotely. The other 99% get to come back to an office with noticeably fewer coworkers.
The drivers aren't employees, so they don't count in the layoff numbers. The people who got laid off were the employees. Uber contains multitudes.
'Simpler and faster' — the press release phrase that means 'we have fewer people now and we'd prefer not to discuss it further.'
captionsJa: 「よりシンプルで速く」なるために10%カット。その10%の仕事が誰に行くかは、まだ計算中。
小規模チームがほぼ半減。4人チームが2人になって、仕事は4人分のまま。シンプルじゃなくて、文句を言う人が減っただけ。
リモート継続が認められるのは全体の1%。残りの99%はオフィスに戻る。ただし同僚は目に見えて減っている。
ドライバーは「従業員」じゃないので、レイオフの数には入らない。レイオフされたのは社員だけ。Uberという会社、いろいろ含んでいる。
「シンプルで速く」というプレスリリース用語の意味：人が減った。それ以上の質問はご遠慮ください。
candidates.newsEn: Uber announced it will cut approximately 10% of its global workforce as part of a company restructuring aimed at becoming 'simpler and faster.' The company said small teams will be reduced by nearly half, and only about 1% of the total workforce will be allowed to continue working fully remotely. No specific division or role was named as the primary target of cuts.

ironyEn.contradiction: Uber's core business is connecting people who need to get somewhere with people who can take them there. The internal staff — the people designing and running that system — just got 10% smaller.
ironyEn.absurdity: 'Simpler and faster' is doing a lot of work in that press release. The company will be simpler in the sense that it now has fewer employees. Whether that makes it faster is a next-quarter problem.
ironyEn.outside: Uber's drivers have never been classified as employees in most US jurisdictions, which means the people actually doing the rides aren't counted in the 10%. Only the people in offices are.

ironyEn.contradiction: The company that built a platform to help people avoid inconvenience is now requiring its remaining 99% of remote workers to come back to the office — on the same day it announced layoffs.
ironyEn.absurdity: Small teams are being cut by nearly half. Which means if you were on a four-person team, there are now two of you. 'Simpler and faster' is one way to put it.
ironyEn.outside: Tech industry layoffs in 2024 and 2025 were supposed to be a correction. In 2026, Uber is still correcting. At some point, the correction is just the shape of the company.

editorial.thread: 今日の5本を貫く糸は「言葉と現実がもう離婚している」。湖の名前、1ドル硬貨、効率化、産休保護——どれも「言い方だけが正しい」話。
editorial.titleEn: A Dollar Worth $1.55, a Lake With Two Names, and Other American Innovations
editorial.subtitleEn: The US is streamlining. The results are something.
editorial.titleJa: 1ドル硬貨を1.55ドルで売る国の話
titleAltJa: 「レイク・アメリカ」に改名して、湖はカナダに半分残ったままだった話
「シンプルで速い会社になります」と言いながら10%を切った人たちに今日会った
editorial.leadJa: 1ドル硬貨を1.55ドルで売る国があります。アメリカです。そして今日、その国では湖の名前を変えて、税金を集める人を解雇して、産休中の人にレイオフを伝えて、「シンプルになります」と言いながら社員を10%切りました。おかしいな〜。
editorial.introEn:
Five stories today. Each one involves someone saying a word and expecting reality to comply.

A lake was renamed. The lake didn't move. A coin worth one dollar is being sold for $1.55. The dollar didn't get stronger. The IRS fired its auditors. Taxes got harder to collect. Uber wants to be "simpler." Someone else will do the work.

Here's your forecast: if you've ever felt like you said the right thing and the world still didn't cooperate — today's news proves you're not alone. The most powerful institutions on the planet are in the same situation. Call it a solidarity Wednesday. Whatever you're carrying, you're at least carrying it more honestly than the US Mint right now.
editorial.introJa:
今日、「1ドル」と書いてあるものを1.55ドルで売っているニュースを読みました。

ただの硬貨の話かと思ったら、続きがあった。オンタリオ湖が「レイク・アメリカ」になっていて、IRSが監査スタッフを削減したら税収が減って、育休中の女性がレイオフされていて、Uberが「シンプルで速くなります」と言いながら全体の10%を切っていた。

今日の5本、全部「言葉と現実が別々に動いている」話なんです。名前を変えても湖は動かない。「ビジネス上の判断」と書けば違法にならない。「効率化」と呼べば10%減でも前向きに聞こえる。

ということで、今日の占いです。
「正しいことしてるのに、なんか報われないな」って感じてる人、たぶんあなたが正しいんですよ。言葉だけ整えて現実を動かそうとしてる人が、今日だけでこんなにいる。そっちが多数派で、あなたは誠実な少数側にいる。
少なくとも今日はね。
editorial.quipEn: Today's theme: America keeps changing the label. The contents remain the same.
editorial.quipJa: 名前を変えても、湖はそこにある。額面を変えても、1ドルは1ドル。言い方だけ正しくなっても、現実はちゃんと残ってる。
notesEn: Apple renamed Lake Ontario 'Lake America' for US users, following a Trump executive order. Canada still calls it Lake Ontario. The lake, for its part, has not commented.
The IRS cut its auditing staff to reduce government waste. An Inspector General report now shows tax enforcement collections dropped sharply as a result. Efficiency, achieved.
The US Mint is selling $1 Trump coins for $1.55 each. If you buy 25, you spend $61 and get $25 worth of spending money. The other $36 is apparently the patriotism surcharge.

Multiple women have reported being laid off while on maternity leave. Employment lawyers confirm it's often legal, as long as the employer calls it a business decision. The naming convention matters more than the timing.
Uber is cutting 10% of its workforce to become 'simpler and faster.' Small teams will be cut nearly in half. The remaining employees will move faster, presumably because they have to.
xJa: Appleがオンタリオ湖をアメリカ国内のMapsアプリで「レイク・アメリカ」に改名。カナダ側の地図には今日も「オンタリオ湖」と書いてある。湖は動いていない。
IRS（米国歳入庁）が監査スタッフを削減したら税収が激減していたことが判明。「税金を集める人を解雇したら税金が集まらなくなった」というレポートが今日出ました。
米造幣局がトランプ大統領の1ドル硬貨を1.55ドル以上で販売中。25枚買うと61ドル取られ、使うと25ドルにしかならない。差額36ドルが「愛国心」の値段らしい。
育休中にレイオフされた女性が複数。「ビジネス上の判断」と言えば合法というのがアメリカの雇用法で、つまり理由の書き方さえ正しければ通る。言葉、重すぎる。
Uberが「シンプルで速くなる」と言いながら従業員の10%を削減。小規模チームはほぼ半減、リモート継続は1%のみ。残り90%がシンプルに2倍働く。
raidEn: Apple changed the name. Canada did not change the lake. There's a lesson here about the limits of executive orders.
The Inspector General found that firing the auditors reduced auditing. I respect the commitment to documenting the obvious.
A dollar coin sold for $2.44. The government has found a way to make inflation feel premium.
"It was a business decision, unrelated to the leave" is doing a lot of heavy lifting in a lot of HR emails right now.
1% of staff gets to keep working remotely. Which means someone in leadership had a very good week and a very specific reason to come back to the office.
raidJa: 「地図の名前を変えたら湖が変わる」と思っていたとしたら、なかなかロマンチックな行政命令ですよね。記事、すごく面白かったです。

editorial.fullEn:
# A Dollar Worth $1.55, a Lake With Two Names, and Other American Innovations

## Today's Forecast

Five stories today. Each one involves someone saying a word and expecting reality to comply.

A lake was renamed. The lake didn't move. A coin worth one dollar is being sold for $1.55. The dollar didn't get stronger. The IRS fired its auditors. Taxes got harder to collect. Uber wants to be "simpler." Someone else will do the work.

Here's your forecast: if you've ever felt like you said the right thing and the world still didn't cooperate — today's news proves you're not alone. The most powerful institutions on the planet are in the same situation. Call it a solidarity Wednesday. Whatever you're carrying, you're at least carrying it more honestly than the US Mint right now.

---

## 1. Apple Renames Lake Ontario 'Lake America' Because an Executive Order Said So

*The Guardian US — [source](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/sep/02/apple-maps-renames-lake-ontario-lake-america)*

Apple has renamed Lake Ontario as 'Lake America' for US users of its Maps app, following an executive order from President Trump issued amid his trade dispute with Canada. The lake sits on the border between the US and Canada and has been called Lake Ontario for centuries. The name change applies only to the US version of Apple Maps.

**Why It's Funny**

Apple renamed Lake Ontario 'Lake America' for US users. The lake is on the border between the US and Canada. Canada still calls it Lake Ontario. The fish have not been informed of the change, and continue to swim through both jurisdictions without documentation. The executive order worked perfectly. The geography just didn't read it.

**Say It Out Loud**

> Apple changed the name of a lake. Canada still has the lake.

---

## 2. IRS Fired Its Auditors. Turns Out, Auditors Were the Ones Collecting Taxes.

*NPR News — [source](https://www.npr.org/2026/09/02/nx-s1-5954022/irs-tax-collection-job-reductions)*

The IRS significantly cut its auditing staff last year as part of broader federal workforce reductions. An Inspector General report now shows that tax collections from enforcement efforts have plummeted as a direct result. Consumer and fiscal watchdog groups warn the shortfall could add substantially to the federal deficit.

**Why It's Funny**

The IRS fired a significant portion of its auditing staff last year. An Inspector General then wrote a report explaining what happened to tax collections afterward. The report's conclusion — that collecting less taxes leads to collecting less taxes — is now officially documented, in writing, for anyone who needs that confirmed. The report runs several pages. The core finding did not.

**Say It Out Loud**

> We fired the tax collectors to save money. We are now saving even more money by not collecting taxes.

---

## 3. US Mint Sells $1 Trump Coins for $1.55 Each, Which Is Not How a Dollar Works

*CBS News US — [source](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-1-dollar-coins-us-mint-sale/)*

The US Mint has begun selling President Donald J. Trump $1 coins, priced at $1.55 per coin at minimum. A package of 25 coins costs $61, while 100 coins cost $154.50, making the per-coin price range from $1.545 to $2.44 depending on quantity. The coins have a face value of one dollar.

**Why It's Funny**

The US Mint is selling $1 Trump coins for $1.55 each, minimum. At the 25-coin package price, you spend $61 and walk away with $25 of purchasing power. The remaining $36 is described nowhere on the product page. The coin says '$1' on its face. The checkout says '$2.44.' Somewhere between those two numbers is the most honest summary of 2026 I've seen all week.

**Say It Out Loud**

> The US government is selling a dollar for $1.55. Inflation, but make it patriotic.

---

## 4. Laid Off While on Maternity Leave. It's Legal. It Happens More Than You Think.

*CNBC Top News — [source](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/02/getting-laid-off-on-maternity-leave.html)*

Several women have reported being laid off by their employers while on maternity leave. Legal experts note that in many US states, this practice is technically lawful as long as the layoff is framed as a business decision rather than a response to the pregnancy or leave itself. Employment attorneys say the line between legal restructuring and illegal discrimination can be difficult to prove in court.

**Why It's Funny**

Several women were laid off while on maternity leave. Employment lawyers explained that this is frequently legal, provided the employer frames it as a business decision rather than a response to the leave itself. So the protection exists. The gap between the protection and what actually happens — that also exists. Both are real. Only one of them shows up on the paperwork.

**Say It Out Loud**

> Great news: you had a baby. Also: we've restructured. Unrelated.

---

## 5. Uber Cuts 10% of Staff to Move 'Simpler and Faster,' Starting With the Humans

*CNBC Top News — [source](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/02/uber-to-cut-10percent-of-workforce-in-bid-to-move-simpler-and-faster.html)*

Uber announced it will cut approximately 10% of its global workforce as part of a company restructuring aimed at becoming 'simpler and faster.' The company said small teams will be reduced by nearly half, and only about 1% of the total workforce will be allowed to continue working fully remotely. No specific division or role was named as the primary target of cuts.

**Why It's Funny**

Uber announced it will cut 10% of its global workforce to become 'simpler and faster.' Small teams will be nearly halved. Fully remote work will be permitted for roughly 1% of employees. The press release described this as streamlining. The people whose work will now be done by fewer people may find a different word for it. Probably not in a press release.

**Say It Out Loud**

> Uber laid off 10% of staff to get 'simpler and faster.' The math on who does their work is still loading.

---

## Today's Punchline

> Today's theme: America keeps changing the label. The contents remain the same.
editorial.fullJa:
# 1ドル硬貨を1.55ドルで売る国の話

## 今日を占うよ〜

今日、「1ドル」と書いてあるものを1.55ドルで売っているニュースを読みました。

ただの硬貨の話かと思ったら、続きがあった。オンタリオ湖が「レイク・アメリカ」になっていて、IRSが監査スタッフを削減したら税収が減って、育休中の女性がレイオフされていて、Uberが「シンプルで速くなります」と言いながら全体の10%を切っていた。

今日の5本、全部「言葉と現実が別々に動いている」話なんです。名前を変えても湖は動かない。「ビジネス上の判断」と書けば違法にならない。「効率化」と呼べば10%減でも前向きに聞こえる。

ということで、今日の占いです。
「正しいことしてるのに、なんか報われないな」って感じてる人、たぶんあなたが正しいんですよ。言葉だけ整えて現実を動かそうとしてる人が、今日だけでこんなにいる。そっちが多数派で、あなたは誠実な少数側にいる。
少なくとも今日はね。

---

## 1. Apple Renames Lake Ontario 'Lake America' Because an Executive Order Said So

*The Guardian US（[記事](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/sep/02/apple-maps-renames-lake-ontario-lake-america)）*

トランプ大統領の行政命令を受け、Appleはカナダとアメリカの国境にあるオンタリオ湖をアメリカ国内のMapsアプリ上で「レイク・アメリカ」に改名した。

**どこが笑える？**

Appleがアメリカ国内のMapsアプリでオンタリオ湖を「レイク・アメリカ」に改名しました。カナダとアメリカの国境にある湖で、カナダ側では今日も「オンタリオ湖」と表示されています。湖の魚は、両方の名前のついた水の中を今日も普通に泳いでいる。

行政命令で地形の名前が変わるなら、次は「大西洋はトランプ・オーシャン」でも誰も驚けないじゃないですか。驚けない自分に気づいた瞬間、ちょっと怖くなりました。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> Appleが湖の名前を変えた。湖はカナダにまだある。

---

## 2. IRS Fired Its Auditors. Turns Out, Auditors Were the Ones Collecting Taxes.

*NPR News（[記事](https://www.npr.org/2026/09/02/nx-s1-5954022/irs-tax-collection-job-reductions)）*

監察総監のレポートにより、IRS（米国歳入庁）が監査スタッフを大幅削減した結果、税務執行による徴収額が急減していたことが明らかになった。

**どこが笑える？**

IRS（米国歳入庁）が監査スタッフを大幅に削減した。で、監察総監のレポートが出た。内容は「監査する人を減らしたら、監査される量が減った」。そのレポート、何ページあったんだろう。

これ、家計でやったら「節約しようと思って収入源を断った」ですよ。でも政府がやると「連邦政府の人員改革」という名前がつく。名前だけ見ると、すごくかっこいいんですよね。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 節税のために税金を集める人を解雇した。おかげで税金がさらに集まらなくなった。

---

## 3. US Mint Sells $1 Trump Coins for $1.55 Each, Which Is Not How a Dollar Works

*CBS News US（[記事](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-1-dollar-coins-us-mint-sale/)）*

米造幣局がトランプ大統領の肖像を刻んだ1ドル硬貨を発売。25枚セットで61ドル（1枚あたり約2.44ドル）から販売されており、額面の1.55倍以上の価格設定となっている。

**どこが笑える？**

米造幣局がトランプ大統領の1ドル硬貨を発売しました。値段は1枚1.55ドルから。25枚セットだと61ドル。使えるのは25ドル分。

残りの36ドルは何かというと、商品ページには書いていません。硬貨には「1ドル」と刻んである。レジは「2.44ドル」と言う。どちらかが嘘をついている。たぶん、硬貨のほうです。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 政府が1ドルを1.55ドルで売っている。インフレ、愛国心でラッピング。

---

## 4. Laid Off While on Maternity Leave. It's Legal. It Happens More Than You Think.

*CNBC Top News（[記事](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/02/getting-laid-off-on-maternity-leave.html)）*

育児休暇中にレイオフされた女性が複数おり、CNBCの報道によれば、こうした解雇は違法ではなく、実態として広く行われている可能性がある。

**どこが笑える？**

育休中にレイオフされた女性が複数いて、CNBCが報じました。雇用弁護士によると、「ビジネス上の判断」として処理すれば、多くの州で合法らしいです。

産休という「会社の制度を正しく使っている期間」に、同じ会社が「あなたはいらなくなりました」と伝える。保護はある。ただその保護と現実のあいだに、書面には残らないすき間がある。そこに落ちた人の話が今日出ていた。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> おめでとうございます、出産しました。あと、組織再編しました。無関係です。

---

## 5. Uber Cuts 10% of Staff to Move 'Simpler and Faster,' Starting With the Humans

*CNBC Top News（[記事](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/02/uber-to-cut-10percent-of-workforce-in-bid-to-move-simpler-and-faster.html)）*

Uberが全従業員の約10%を削減すると発表。「よりシンプルかつ迅速に動く」ことを目的とするとしており、小規模チームはほぼ半減、リモートワーク継続を認められるのは全体の約1%にとどまる。

**どこが笑える？**

Uberが全従業員の約10%を削減すると発表。理由は「よりシンプルかつ迅速に動くため」。小規模チームはほぼ半減、リモートワーク継続は全体の1%のみ。

「シンプルで速い」という言葉を選んだ人は、残された人が10%分の仕事を引き受けることを「シンプル」と呼んでいる。言葉の使い方として、かなり勇気がある。残された人の感想は、たぶんプレスリリースには載らない言葉で表現されると思います。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 「よりシンプルで速く」なるために10%カット。その10%の仕事が誰に行くかは、まだ計算中。

---

## 今日のまとめジョーク/パンチライン

> 名前を変えても、湖はそこにある。額面を変えても、1ドルは1ドル。言い方だけ正しくなっても、現実はちゃんと残ってる。

今日も読んでくれてありがとうございます。また明日の朝、ここで。
